adjoining /əˈʤɔɪnɪŋ/ 毗邻的 structures /ˈstrəkʧərz/ 结构

088

In the aftermath of this incredible misfortune, the pieces of the puzzle began to be put in place.

在经历了这场令人难以置信的不幸之后，拼图的碎片开始被拼凑起来。

aftermath /ˈæftərˌmæθ/ 后果 incredible /ˌɪnˈkrɛdəbəl/ 极好的 misfortune /mɪsˈfɔrʧən/ 不幸

089

Shortly before 8∶00 a.m. on September 11, 2001, three commercial airliners were hijacked from Logan Airport in Boston, Massachusetts.

2001年9月11日上午8时00分左右，马萨诸塞州波士顿洛根机场三架商业客机被劫持。

shortly /ˈʃɔrtli/ 不久 commercial /kəˈmərʃəl/ 商业的 airliners /ˈɛˌrlaɪnərz/ 客机 hijacked /ˈhaɪˌʤækt/ 被劫持 airport /ˈɛrˌpɔrt/ 飞机场

090

All were transcontinental flights with passengers destined for California and their full fuel tanks provided the ammunition critical to the mission of the hijackers.

所有航班都是横贯大陆的航班，载有乘客前往加利福尼亚州，其满载的油箱为劫机者的任务提供了至关重要的弹药。

transcontinental /ˌtrænzˌkɑnɪˈnɛnəl/ 横贯大陆的 flights /flaɪts/ 航班 passengers /ˈpæsənʤərz/ 乘客 destined /ˈdɛstɪnd/ 注定的 california /ˌkæləˈfɔrnjə/ 加利福尼亚州

091

Authorities speculate that the pilots were assassinated and their places taken by the terrorists who had had flight training.

当局推测飞行员被暗杀，他们的位置被接受过飞行训练的恐怖分子所取代。

authorities /əˈθɔrətiz/ 当局 speculate /ˈspɛkjəˌleɪt/ 推测 assassinated /əˈsæsəˌneɪtəd/ 被暗杀 terrorists /ˈtɛrəˌrɪsts/ 恐怖分子 training /ˈtreɪnɪŋ/ 训练

092

In all, there were 157 passengers and crew on the two planes.

两架飞机上共有 157 名乘客和机组人员。

passengers /ˈpæsənʤərz/ 乘客

093

The third plane crashed in Pennsylvania killing 45 passengers and crew.

第三架飞机在宾夕法尼亚州坠毁，造成 45 名乘客和机组人员死亡。

crashed /kræʃt/ 坠毁 pennsylvania /ˌpɛnsəlˈveɪnjə/ 宾夕法尼亚州 killing /ˈkɪlɪŋ/ 杀戮 passengers /ˈpæsənʤərz/ 乘客

094

A number of the hostages managed to use their cellular telephones to call their families to say goodbye.

一些人质设法用手机给家人打电话告别。

hostages /ˈhɑstəʤəz/ 人质 managed /ˈmænɪʤd/ 管理的 cellular /ˈsɛljələr/ 细胞的 telephones /ˈtɛləˌfoʊnz/ 电话 families /ˈfæməliz/ 家庭

095

Everything occurred in such a short period of time that, other than alerting a handful of people that there were some hijackings, no one had any idea why.

一切都发生在如此短的时间内，除了提醒少数人发生了一些劫持之外，没有人知道为什么。

everything /ˈɛvriˌθɪŋ/ 一切 occurred /əˈkərd/ 发生 alerting /əˈlərtɪŋ/ 警报 handful /ˈhændˌfʊl/ 少数 hijackings /ˈhaɪˌʤækɪŋz/ 劫持

096

The dilemma was that there were no warnings, no demands for ransom, and no hints that this bright, sunny September morning was about to become a day that will live forever in the minds of those who witnessed the tragedy.

困境在于，没有任何警告，没有勒索赎金，也没有任何迹象表明这个九月阳光明媚的早晨将成为永远活在目睹这场悲剧的人们心中的一天。

dilemma /dɪˈlɛmə/ 困境 warnings /ˈwɔrnɪŋz/ 警告 demands /dɪˈmændz/ 需求 morning /ˈmɔrnɪŋ/ 早晨 forever /fərˈɛvər/ 永远

097

It will be years before the final toll of damage will be known.

最终损失人数还需要数年时间才能得知。

098

To consolidate information, compute the financial losses, designate a monetary value for loss of life, fill the void left on the terrain, to make sense of this misfortune intended to undermine the foundation of America is a formidable assignment.

整合信息、计算经济损失、确定生命损失的货币价值、填补地形上留下的空白、理解这场旨在破坏美国基础的不幸是一项艰巨的任务。

consolidate /kənˈsɑlɪˌdeɪt/ 巩固 information /ˌɪnˌfɔrˈmeɪʃən/ 信息 compute /kəmˈpjut/ 计算 financial /ˌfaɪˈnænʃəl/ 金融的 designate /ˈdɛzɪgˌneɪt/ 指定

099

We do know that destruction of the World Trade Center cost the lives of more than three thousand innocent people in the buildings, in the hijacked airplanes, and in the surrounding streets.

我们确实知道，世贸中心的毁坏导致大楼内、被劫持的飞机和周围街道上三千多名无辜者丧生。

destruction /dɪˈstrəkʃən/ 破坏 trade /treɪd/ 贸易 thousand /ˈθaʊzənd/ 千 innocent /ˈɪnəsənt/ 清白的 buildings /ˈbɪldɪŋz/ 建筑物

100

Who can erase the mental images of those planes smashing into the twin towers, Who is unable to visualize the spectacle of terrified men and women jumping to their doom, How can those of us who observed the collapse of the buildings fail to dwell on the loss of life caused by men,cowards, who lacked the fortitud to proclaim war on their alleged enemy, Today, October 22, 2001, nine more corpses were discovered in the rubbl, the first such discovery in several weeks.

谁能抹去那些飞机撞向双子塔的脑海里的画面，谁无法想象那些惊恐万状的男男女女跳向末日的景象，我们这些目睹建筑物倒塌的人怎么能不去思考那些缺乏向所谓的敌人宣战的勇气的男人、懦夫所造成的生命损失呢，今天，2001年10月22日，在废墟中又发现了九具尸体，这是数年来首次发现这样的尸体。几周。

smashing /sˈmæʃɪŋ/ 粉碎 visualize /ˈvɪʒwəˌlaɪz/ 可视化 spectacle /ˈspɛktəkəl/ 奇观 terrified /ˈtɛrəˌfaɪd/ 害怕 jumping /ˈʤəmpɪŋ/ 跳跃

101

This may seem trivial when one considers the multitude of people who died.

考虑到死者人数之多，这一点似乎微不足道。

trivial /ˈtrɪviəl/ 琐碎的 considers /kənˈsɪdərz/ 考虑 multitude /ˈməltəˌtud/ 民众

102

However, the fatalities aren't the only victims of this tragic event.

然而，死亡者并不是这一悲惨事件的唯一受害者。

however /ˌhaʊˈɛvər/ 然而 fatalities /fəˈtælɪtiz/ 死亡人数 victims /ˈvɪktɪmz/ 受害者

103

Their families, friends, and colleagues need closure.

他们的家人、朋友和同事需要了结。

families /ˈfæməliz/ 家庭 friends /frɛndz/ 朋友们 colleagues /ˈkɑligz/ 同事 closure /ˈkloʊʒər/ 关闭

104

They need to know with certainty that their loved ones are dead and they need to bury the remains.

他们需要确切地知道他们的亲人已经去世，他们需要埋葬遗体。

certainty /ˈsərtənti/ 肯定 remains /rɪˈmeɪnz/ 遗迹

105

Unfortunately,most of the casualties will probably never be found because the heat produced by the ignition of jet fuel and the damage incurred by the impact would have instantaneously vaporized everything and everyone in the immediate vicinity.

不幸的是，大多数伤亡人员可能永远不会被发现，因为喷气燃料点燃产生的热量以及撞击造成的损害会立即蒸发附近的一切和每个人。

unfortunately /ənˈfɔrʧənətli/ 很遗憾 casualties /ˈkæʒəwəltiz/ 伤亡 probably /ˈprɑbəˌbli/ 大概 because /bɪˈkəz/ 因为 produced /prəˈdust/ 产生的

106

Others, in the buildings or on the streets as the towers collapsed are under so much debris that their bodies may not be found for months.

塔楼倒塌时，其他人则在建筑物内或街道上，埋在大量废墟下，以至于他们的尸体可能几个月都找不到。

buildings /ˈbɪldɪŋz/ 建筑物 streets /strits/ 街道 collapsed /kəˈlæpst/ 崩溃了

107

The list of buildings collapsed and damaged includes all seven buildings of the W.

倒塌和损坏的建筑物清单包括 W. 的所有七座建筑物。

buildings /ˈbɪldɪŋz/ 建筑物 collapsed /kəˈlæpst/ 崩溃了 damaged /ˈdæmɪʤd/ 损坏的 includes /ˌɪnˈkludz/ 包括

108

T.

T。

109

C.complex comprising W.

C.复合物包括W.

complex /ˈkɑmplɛks/ 复杂的 comprising /kəmˈpraɪzɪŋ/ 包括

110

T.

T。

111

C.6, the U.

C.6、U.

112

S.

S。

113

Customs House to the north; W.

北边是海关大楼； W.

customs /ˈkəstəmz/ 海关

114

T.

T。

115

C.3, the 22 story Marriott World Trade Center Hotel just west of Tower Two; W.

C.3，22层的万豪世贸中心酒店，位于二号塔西侧； W.

marriott /ˈmɛriət/ 万豪酒店 trade /treɪd/ 贸易 tower /taʊər/ 塔

116

T.

T。

117

C.4 and 5, the Plaza Buildings, and One Liberty Plaza, a 54 story, 743 foot high building to the east.

C.4 和 5，广场大楼，以及东边一栋 54 层、743 英尺高的建筑自由广场一号。

buildings /ˈbɪldɪŋz/ 建筑物 liberty /ˈlɪbərˌti/ 自由 building /ˈbɪldɪŋ/ 建筑

118

Firefighters and recovery workers remain on the scene.

消防队员和救援人员仍在现场。

firefighters /ˈfaɪərˌfaɪtərz/ 消防员 recovery /rɪˈkəvəri/ 恢复 workers /ˈwərkərz/ 工人

119

The fires still smolder beneath the ruins.

废墟下的大火仍在闷烧。

smolder /sˈmoʊldər/ 闷烧 beneath /bɪˈniθ/ 下面

120

The American spirit has been bruised and the land has been scarred.

美国精神已受到重创，土地已是伤痕累累。

bruised /bruzd/ 擦伤的 scarred /skɑrd/ 伤痕累累的

121

The citizens of this powerful nation now realize just how fragile and vulnerable their country is.

这个强大国家的公民现在意识到他们的国家是多么脆弱和脆弱。

citizens /ˈsɪtɪzənz/ 公民 powerful /ˈpaʊərfəl/ 强大的 realize /ˈriəˌlaɪz/ 意识到 fragile /ˈfræʤəl/ 脆弱的 vulnerable /ˈvəlnərəbəl/ 易受伤害的

122

Nevertheless,they are defiant.

尽管如此，他们还是挑衅的。

nevertheless /ˌnɛvərðəˈlɛs/ 尽管如此 defiant /dɪˈfaɪənt/ 挑衅的

123

They do not consider themselves easy prey for terrorists.

他们认为自己不容易成为恐怖分子的猎物。

consider /kənˈsɪdər/ 考虑 terrorists /ˈtɛrəˌrɪsts/ 恐怖分子

124

They are still optimistic about their place in today's world.

他们仍然对自己在当今世界的地位持乐观态度。

optimistic /ˌɑptɪˈmɪstɪk/ 乐观的

125

They assert that the nightmare visited upon them will be visited upon the perpetrators of this cowardly act.

他们断言，降临到他们身上的噩梦也将降临到这种懦弱行为的肇事者身上。

nightmare /ˈnaɪtˌmɛr/ 恶梦 visited /ˈvɪzɪtɪd/ 访问过 perpetrators /ˈpərpəˌtreɪtərz/ 肇事者 cowardly /ˈkaʊərdli/ 胆小

126

The World Trade Center is no more.

世界贸易中心已不复存在。

trade /treɪd/ 贸易

127

The dream of an international axis of business, once a reality,will be revised.

国际商业轴的梦想一旦成为现实，就会被修改。

international /ˌɪnərˈnæʃənɑl/ 国际的 business /ˈbɪznɪs/ 商业 reality /ˌriˈæləˌti/ 现实 revised /rɪˈvaɪzd/ 修改

128

Maybe having one place that is so prominent will also be rethought.

也许拥有一个如此突出的地方也会被重新考虑。

prominent /ˈprɑmənənt/ 著名的 rethought /riˈθɔt/ 重新思考

129

Whatever the outcome, this massacre has served to strengthen the resolve of a mighty nation.

无论结果如何，这场屠杀都坚定了一个强大国家的决心。

whatever /ˌwəˈtɛvər/ 任何 outcome /ˈaʊtˌkəm/ 结果 massacre /ˈmæsəkər/ 屠杀 strengthen /ˈstrɛŋθən/ 加强 resolve /riˈzɑlv/ 解决

130

The dream and dreamers will survive.

梦想和梦想家将会生存。

dreamers /ˈdrimərz/ 梦想家 survive /sərˈvaɪv/ 存活

docs.title: Sex Role Stereotypes
docs.text:
原文链接：Part 1 / Part 2

复习方式：先读英文，再看译文，最后只背本句下面的词和短语。

001

During my career as a Canadian female teacher, I observed many instances of sex role stereotyping throughout the western culture.

在我作为加拿大女教师的职业生涯中，我观察到整个西方文化中许多性别角色刻板印象的例子。

teacher /ˈtiʧər/ 老师 observed /əbˈzərvd/ 观察到的 instances /ˈɪnstənsɪz/ 实例 stereotyping /ˈstɛrioʊˌtaɪpɪŋ/ 刻板印象 western /ˈwɛstərn/ 西

002

I was always amazed how quickly young children adopted the cultural values.

我总是惊讶于小孩子们如此迅速地接受了文化价值观。

quickly /kˈwɪkli/ 迅速地 children /ˈʧɪldrən/ 孩子们 adopted /əˈdɑptəd/ 通过 cultural /ˈkəlʧərəl/ 文化

003

The topic is one of major concerns in the western world, yet there are those people who would ask you to believe that it is not a major issue.

这个话题是西方世界最关心的问题之一，但有些人会要求你相信这不是一个主要问题。

concerns /kənˈsərnz/ 担忧 western /ˈwɛstərn/ 西 believe /bɪˈliv/ 相信

004

People who wish to ignore the situation do not welcome discussions on the topic of gender bias.

那些想要忽视这种情况的人不欢迎关于性别偏见话题的讨论。

situation /ˌsɪʧuˈeɪʃən/ 情况 welcome /ˈwɛlkəm/ 欢迎 discussions /dɪˈskəʃənz/ 讨论

005

This type of person evokes an analogy of an ostrich that buries its head in the sand to ignore a problem by avoiding it.

这种人就像鸵鸟一样，把头埋在沙子里，通过回避问题来忽视问题。

analogy /əˈnæləʤi/ 类比 ostrich /ˈɔstrɪʧ/ 鸵鸟 problem /ˈprɑbləm/ 问题 avoiding /əˈvɔɪdɪŋ/ 回避

006

Although many of my comments may seem cynical, I give you assurance that they are based on my observation of western society for a number of years.

尽管我的许多评论可能显得愤世嫉俗，但我向您保证，它们是基于我多年来对西方社会的观察。

although /ˌɔlˈðoʊ/ 虽然 comments /ˈkɑmɛnts/ 评论 cynical /ˈsɪnɪkəl/ 愤世嫉俗的 assurance /əˈʃʊrəns/ 保证 observation /ˌɑbzərˈveɪʃən/ 观察

007

It might be interesting and informative to compare the western world in this respect with eastern cultures.

在这方面将西方世界与东方文化进行比较可能会很有趣且信息丰富。

interesting /ˈɪntəˌrɛstɪŋ/ 有趣的 informative /ˌɪnˈfɔrmətɪv/ 信息丰富的 compare /kəmˈpɛr/ 比较 western /ˈwɛstərn/ 西 respect /rɪˈspɛkt/ 尊重

008

Many studies have been done and the breakdown of reasons examined to determine why gender roles play an important part in the selection of successful candidates for positions in many vocations.

人们已经进行了许多研究，并对原因进行了详细分析，以确定为什么性别角色在许多职业职位的成功候选人选择中发挥着重要作用。

studies /ˈstədiz/ 研究 breakdown /ˈbreɪkˌdaʊn/ 分解 reasons /ˈrizənz/ 原因 examined /ɪgˈzæmənd/ 检查过 determine /dɪˈtərmən/ 决定

009

These studies have made little impact on diminishing the prevalence of candidates being selected more for their gender than their qualifications.

这些研究对于减少候选人因性别而非资历而被选拔的现象影响甚微。

studies /ˈstədiz/ 研究 diminishing /dɪˈmɪnɪʃɪŋ/ 递减 prevalence /ˈprɛvələns/ 患病率 candidates /ˈkænədɪts/ 候选人 selected /səˈlɛktɪd/ 已选择

010

Since the people responsible for hiring people to work with them, often hire people similar to themselves, it seems like they are looking for a clone or a duplicate of themselves.

由于负责雇用与他们一起工作的人的人经常雇用与自己相似的人，因此他们似乎正在寻找自己的克隆或复制品。

responsible /riˈspɑnsəbəl/ 负责任的 similar /ˈsɪmələr/ 相似的 duplicate /ˈdupləˌkeɪt/ 复制

011

Females often become quite indignant when positions that they are well suited for are awarded to males and ambiguous reasons given to explain why.

当女性非常适合的职位被授予男性，并且给出的解释含糊其辞时，女性常常会变得非常愤怒。

females /ˈfiˌmeɪlz/ 女性 indignant /ˌɪnˈdɪgnənt/ 愤怒 positions /pəˈzɪʃənz/ 职位 awarded /əˈwɔrdɪd/ 授予 ambiguous /æmˈbɪgjuəs/ 模糊的

012

Is it any wonder that attempts to sue corporations for using unfair hiring and promotion practices are applauded, On the other hand, companies who exhibit fair hiring practices need to be commended for doing so.

起诉使用不公平招聘和晋升做法的公司的尝试会受到赞扬，这有什么奇怪的吗？另一方面，表现出公平招聘做法的公司应该因此而受到赞扬。

attempts /əˈtɛmpts/ 尝试 corporations /ˌkɔrpərˈeɪʃənz/ 公司 promotion /pərˈmoʊʃən/ 晋升 practices /ˈpræktɪsɪz/ 实践 applauded /əˈplɔdɪd/ 鼓掌

013

It has been common in the western world for people to presume that certain professions belong almost exclusively to one gender or the other.

在西方世界，人们普遍认为某些职业几乎完全属于一种性别。

western /ˈwɛstərn/ 西 presume /prɪˈzum/ 怙 certain /ˈsərtən/ 肯定 professions /prəˈfɛʃənz/ 职业 exclusively /ɪkˈsklusɪvli/ 只

014

The work of an electrician, or work with electronics, or repairing of air-conditioning equipment, might be considered to be masculine fields of employment.

电工工作、电子产品工作或空调设备维修工作可能被认为是男性就业领域。

electrician /ɪlɛkˈtrɪʃən/ 电工 electronics /ˌɪˌlɛkˈtrɑnɪks/ 电子产品 repairing /rɪˈpɛrɪŋ/ 修理 air-conditioning /ˈɛrkənˌdɪʃənɪŋ/ 空调 equipment /ɪkˈwɪpmənt/ 设备

015

Nursing and childcare vocations are considered feminine occupations.

护理和育儿职业被认为是女性职业。

nursing /ˈnərsɪŋ/ 护理 childcare /ˈʧaɪldˌkɛr/ 儿童保育 vocations /voʊˈkeɪʃənz/ 职业 considered /kənˈsɪdərd/ 经过考虑的 feminine /ˈfɛmənən/ 女性化的

016

Aviation is another field where people would usually assume that the pilot would be male and the flight attendant would be female, a premise that many times will be invalid.

航空业是另一个领域，人们通常会假设飞行员是男性，空乘人员是女性，但这个前提很多时候都是无效的。

aviation /ˌeɪviˈeɪʃən/ 航空 usually /ˈjuʒəwəli/ 通常 attendant /əˈtɛndənt/ 服务员 premise /ˈprɛmɪs/ 前提 invalid /ˌɪnˈvæləd/ 无效的

017

It will be a major breakthrough when both genders are equally represented in the workforce especially in higher level positions.

当男女在劳动力队伍中，特别是在更高级别的职位上拥有平等的代表权时，这将是一个重大突破。

breakthrough /ˈbreɪkθˌru/ 突破 genders /ˈʤɛndərz/ 性别 equally /ˈikwəli/ 同样地 represented /ˌrɛprɪˈzɛnɪd/ 代表 workforce /ˈwərkˌfɔrs/ 劳动力

018

Some individuals would lead you to believe that it would result in the breakdown of society, as we know it today.

正如我们今天所知，有些人会让你相信这会导致社会崩溃。

individuals /ˌɪndəˈvɪʤəwəlz/ 个人 believe /bɪˈliv/ 相信 breakdown /ˈbreɪkˌdaʊn/ 分解 society /soʊˈsaɪɪti/ 社会

019

At times an attempt to prevent subjective views being used to preclude only males being hired by males has been attempted.

有时，有人试图阻止主观观点被用来排除男性只受男性雇用的情况。

attempt /əˈtɛmpt/ 试图 prevent /prɪˈvɛnt/ 防止 subjective /səˈbʤɛktɪv/ 主观 preclude /prɪˈklud/ 排除 attempted /əˈtɛmptəd/ 尝试过

020

Laws or policy that attempt to rectify the situation have not been successful in diminishing the problem.

试图纠正这种情况的法律或政策并没有成功地减少问题。

attempt /əˈtɛmpt/ 试图 rectify /ˈrɛktəˌfaɪ/ 纠正 situation /ˌsɪʧuˈeɪʃən/ 情况 successful /səkˈsɛsfəl/ 成功的 diminishing /dɪˈmɪnɪʃɪŋ/ 递减

021

An attempt to numerically control the number of positions in a corporation by using a quota system to require equal numbers of males and females to be hired usually meets with little success if the attitudes of the people doing the hiring are subjective and preclude the possibility of fair practises being used.

如果招聘人员的态度是主观的并且排除了采用公平做法的可能性，那么通过使用配额制度来要求雇用同等数量的男性和女性来对公司职位数量进行数字控制的尝试通常不会成功。

attempt /əˈtɛmpt/ 试图 numerically /nuˈmɛrɪkli/ 数字上 control /kənˈtroʊl/ 控制 positions /pəˈzɪʃənz/ 职位 corporation /ˌkɔrpərˈeɪʃən/ 公司

022

The empirical evidence shown by the numbers makes it easy to show which companies exemplify fairness and would hinder those who only make a feeble attempt to do so.

数字所显示的经验证据可以很容易地表明哪些公司体现了公平性，并且会阻碍那些仅做出微弱尝试的公司。

empirical /ˌɛmˈpɪrɪkəl/ 经验 evidence /ˈɛvədəns/ 证据 numbers /ˈnəmbərz/ 数字 companies /ˈkəmpəˌniz/ 公司 exemplify /ɪgˈzɛmpləˌfaɪ/ 举例说明

023

If a company does endeavour to incorporate fairness in their hiring practises, they should be eligible for commendation.

如果公司确实努力将公平纳入其招聘实践，他们应该有资格获得表彰。

company /ˈkəmpəˌni/ 公司 endeavour /ɪnˈdɛvər/ 努力 incorporate /ˌɪnˈkɔrpərˌeɪt/ 包含 fairness /ˈfɛrnəs/ 公平 practises /ˈpræktɪsɪz/ 实践

024

A diligent attempt to choose the best person for the position regardless of their gender is only inherent in those companies that can envisage a future with the best possible work force.

只有那些能够设想未来拥有最佳劳动力的公司才会努力选择最适合该职位的人，无论其性别如何。

diligent /ˈdɪlɪʤənt/ 勤奋 attempt /əˈtɛmpt/ 试图 position /pəˈzɪʃən/ 位置 regardless /rəˈgɑrdləs/ 不管 inherent /ˌɪnˈhɛrənt/ 固有

025

A dvertisements depict gender bias while promoting products.

广告在推销产品时描绘了性别偏见。

dvertisements：广告 promoting /prəˈmoʊtɪŋ/ 促进 products /ˈprɑdəkts/ 产品

026

Looking at merchandise displays in any mall will reveal that a picture of a juvenile lad would be near construction equipment while an ad for perfume would likely show a female.

观察任何商场的商品陈列都会发现，建筑设备附近会出现一个少年的照片，而香水广告上可能会出现一个女性。

merchandise /ˈmərʧənˌdaɪz/ 商品 displays /dɪˈspleɪz/ 显示 picture /ˈpɪkʧər/ 图片 juvenile /ˈʤuvəˌnaɪl/ 少年 construction /kənˈstrəkʃən/ 建造

027

The drawback of this seemingly innocent way of displaying merchandise is that they tend to affirm the bias of the individuals who design them.

这种看似无害的商品展示方式的缺点是，它们往往会肯定设计者的偏见。

drawback /ˈdrɔˌbæk/ 退税 seemingly /ˈsimɪŋli/ 似乎 innocent /ˈɪnəsənt/ 清白的 displaying /dɪˈspleɪɪŋ/ 显示 merchandise /ˈmərʧənˌdaɪz/ 商品

028

This is a serious flaw.

这是一个严重的缺陷。

serious /ˈsɪriəs/ 严肃的

029

Maybe the intent was not to be exclusive but that is the end result of the message that is evoked, whether subliminal or overt.

也许意图并不是排他性的，但这就是所唤起的信息的最终结果，无论是潜意识的还是公开的。

exclusive /ɪkˈsklusɪv/ 独家的 message /ˈmɛsɪʤ/ 信息 whether /ˈwɛðər/ 无论 subliminal /səˈblɪmɪnəl/ 潜意识的

030

An alternate way of viewing the world, with either both genders portrayed or neither with the items, may seem bizarre but marketing specialists have been applauded for making the effort to do so.

以另一种方式看待世界，要么描绘出两种性别，要么描绘出物品，这可能看起来很奇怪，但营销专家为此付出的努力受到了赞扬。

alternate /ˈɔltərˌneɪt/ 备用 viewing /vjuɪŋ/ 观看 genders /ˈʤɛndərz/ 性别 portrayed /pɔrˈtreɪd/ 描绘的 neither /ˈniðər/ 两者都不

031

The hypothesis has been suggested that if this practise were widespread it would facilitate a change for the better in the values that are embedded in our society.

有人假设，如果这种做法广泛传播，将有助于我们社会中根深蒂固的价值观发生更好的变化。

hypothesis /haɪˈpɑθəsəs/ 假设 suggested /səˈʤɛstɪd/ 建议 practise /ˈpræktɪs/ 实践 widespread /ˈwaɪdˈsprɛd/ 广泛 facilitate /fəˈsɪləˌteɪt/ 促进

032

When you read a biography in a newspaper in a metropolitan area, you will find that different words are used to describe males and females.

当你在大都市地区的报纸上阅读传记时，你会发现描述男性和女性的词是不同的。

biography /baɪˈɑgrəfi/ 传 newspaper /ˈnuzˌpeɪpər/ 报纸 metropolitan /ˌmɛtrəˈpɑlətən/ 大都市的 different /ˈdɪfərənt/ 不同的 describe /dɪˈskraɪb/ 描述

033

In almost any literary work, personal appearance is seldom mentioned when describing males, but commonly used when a female is the subject of the article.

在几乎所有的文学作品中，描述男性时很少提及个人外表，但当文章的主题是女性时则常用。

literary /ˈlɪtərˌɛri/ 文学的 personal /ˈpərsɪnəl/ 个人的 appearance /əˈpɪrəns/ 外貌 mentioned /ˈmɛnʃənd/ 提及 describing /dɪˈskraɪbɪŋ/ 描述

034

Forms of address that are considered proper to use are also discriminatory.

被认为适合使用的称呼形式也具有歧视性。

address /ˈæˌdrɛs/ 地址 considered /kənˈsɪdərd/ 经过考虑的 discriminatory /dɪˈskrɪmənəˌtɔri/ 歧视性的

035

Males are always referred to as Mr. (except a very young lad might be addressed as Master).

男性总是被称为“先生”（除了非常年轻的小伙子可能被称为“主人”）。

referred /rɪˈfərd/ 提到的 addressed /əˈdrɛst/ 已解决

036

There are several forms of abbreviations to use before the name of a female.

女性名字前可以使用多种形式的缩写。

several /ˈsɛvərəl/ 一些 abbreviations /əˌbriviˈeɪʃənz/ 缩写

037

It is permissible to use Mrs., Miss, or Ms. The choice of abbreviation is by personal preference of the person being addressed but they have different meanings.

允许使用 Mrs.、Miss 或 Ms。缩写的选择取决于被称呼者的个人喜好，但它们具有不同的含义。

permissible /pərˈmɪsəbəl/ 允许的 abbreviation /əˌbriviˈeɪʃən/ 缩写 personal /ˈpərsɪnəl/ 个人的 preference /ˈprɛfərəns/ 偏爱 addressed /əˈdrɛst/ 已解决

038

Mrs. is used to signify a married woman.

Mrs.用来表示已婚妇女。

signify /ˈsɪgnəˌfaɪ/ 表示 married /ˈmɛrid/ 已婚

039

Miss means an unmarried or single woman.

小姐是指未婚或单身女性。

unmarried /ənˈmɛrid/ 未婚

040

Ms. could mean either and is the choice of many women because it does not reveal their marital status.

Ms. 可能意味着其中任何一个，并且是许多女性的选择，因为它不会透露她们的婚姻状况。

because /bɪˈkəz/ 因为 marital /ˈmærətəl/ 婚姻

041

How strange that society feels it is necessary to be able to deduce a woman's marital status from her name by providing this form of definitive identification.

社会认为有必要通过提供这种形式的明确身份证明来从女性的名字中推断出她的婚姻状况，这是多么奇怪啊。

strange /streɪnʤ/ 奇怪的 society /soʊˈsaɪɪti/ 社会 necessary /ˈnɛsəˌsɛri/ 必要的 marital /ˈmærətəl/ 婚姻 providing /prəˈvaɪdɪŋ/ 提供

042

A man could be married or could be a bachelor and one is not able to ascertain his marital status from his name.

一个男人可能已婚，也可能是单身汉，但人们无法从他的名字中确定他的婚姻状况。

married /ˈmɛrid/ 已婚 bachelor /ˈbæʧələr/ 学士 ascertain /ˌæsərˈteɪn/ 探明 marital /ˈmærətəl/ 婚姻

043

Why, then, is it necessary to differentiate between a woman who is married and one who is not, Many of the cases of sexual harassment that are dealt with in corporations are a result of stereotyping.

那么，为什么有必要区分已婚女性和未婚女性呢？公司处理的许多性骚扰案件都是陈规定型观念的结果。

necessary /ˈnɛsəˌsɛri/ 必要的 differentiate /ˌdɪfərˈɛnʧiˌeɪt/ 区分 married /ˈmɛrid/ 已婚 harassment /hərˈæsmənt/ 骚扰 corporations /ˌkɔrpərˈeɪʃənz/ 公司

044

Usually the person who is the alleged harasser is a male who supervises females.

通常，被指控的骚扰者是监督女性的男性。

usually /ˈjuʒəwəli/ 通常 alleged /əˈlɛʤd/ 据称 harasser /hərˈæsər/ 骚扰者 supervises /ˈsupərˌvaɪzɪz/ 监督 females /ˈfiˌmeɪlz/ 女性

045

Males have been taught by society that they are the privileged gender and have power over any female.

社会教导男性，他们是享有特权的性别，拥有凌驾于任何女性之上的权力。

society /soʊˈsaɪɪti/ 社会 privileged /ˈprɪvɪlɪʤd/ 特权

046

This is the basis behind most incidents of harassment.

这是大多数骚扰事件背后的基础。

incidents /ˈɪnsədənts/ 事件 harassment /hərˈæsmənt/ 骚扰

047

How strange that intelligent men feel entitled to take advantage of females in a subordinate position.

聪明的男人觉得自己有权利用处于从属地位的女性，这是多么奇怪啊。

strange /streɪnʤ/ 奇怪的 intelligent /ˌɪnˈtɛləʤənt/ 聪明的 entitled /ɛnˈtaɪtəld/ 有权 advantage /ædˈvæntɪʤ/ 优势 females /ˈfiˌmeɪlz/ 女性

048

To heighten awareness, forums or symposiums are held to enlighten people about the importance of using inclusive language but may people still resist changing.

为了提高认识，举办论坛或研讨会来启发人们使用包容性语言的重要性，但人们可能仍然抵制改变。

heighten /ˈhaɪtən/ 增高 awareness /əˈwɛrnəs/ 意识 symposiums /sɪmˈpoʊziəmz/ 研讨会 enlighten /ˌɛnˈlaɪtən/ 开导 importance /ˌɪmˈpɔrtəns/ 重要性

049

Some people are determined that the word man also includes woman.

有些人认定男人这个词也包括女人。

determined /dɪˈtərmənd/ 决定 includes /ˌɪnˈkludz/ 包括

050

Sometimes the meaning does incorporate women and sometimes it doesnt.

有时这个含义确实包含女性，有时则不然。

sometimes /ˈsəmˌtaɪmz/ 有时 meaning /ˈminɪŋ/ 意义 incorporate /ˌɪnˈkɔrpərˌeɪt/ 包含

051

However, many woman insist that they are never quite sure of the meaning and suggest that the word humanity should be used instead when the intended meaning is both men and women and then there would be no confusion.

然而，许多女性坚持认为，她们从来不太确定其含义，并建议当预期含义同时是男性和女性时，应该使用“人类”一词，这样就不会造成混淆。

however /ˌhaʊˈɛvər/ 然而 meaning /ˈminɪŋ/ 意义 suggest /səˈʤɛst/ 建议 humanity /juˈmænɪti/ 人类 instead /ˌɪnˈstɛd/ 反而

052

It is incomprehensible to others why they refuse to change.

其他人无法理解他们为什么拒绝改变。

incomprehensible /ˌɪŋˌkɑmprəˈhɛnsɪbəl/ 难以理解的

053

A booklet or pamphlet is available for reference in most work places to help people use inclusive language in any writing in the workplace.

大多数工作场所都提供小册子或小册子供参考，以帮助人们在工作场所的任何写作中使用包容性语言。

booklet /ˈbʊklɪt/ 小册子 pamphlet /ˈpæmflət/ 小册子 available /əˈveɪləbəl/ 可用的 reference /ˈrɛfərəns/ 参考 inclusive /ˌɪnˈklusɪv/ 包容性

054

Some government offices have produced a leaflet that can be used by companies that do not have the impetus or the resources to design their own.

一些政府办公室制作了一份传单，可供没有动力或资源自行设计的公司使用。

government /ˈgəvərnmənt/ 政府 offices /ˈɔfəsɪz/ 办公室 produced /prəˈdust/ 产生的 leaflet /ˈliflət/ 传单 companies /ˈkəmpəˌniz/ 公司

055

Studies about gender differences have suggested a hypothesis that females have better verbal skills, while males excel at tasks requiring the ability to visualize.

关于性别差异的研究提出了一个假设，即女性拥有更好的语言能力，而男性则擅长需要想象能力的任务。

studies /ˈstədiz/ 研究 differences /ˈdɪfərənsɪz/ 差异 suggested /səˈʤɛstɪd/ 建议 hypothesis /haɪˈpɑθəsəs/ 假设 females /ˈfiˌmeɪlz/ 女性

056

Conclusions of many of the studies have proved it invalid and found instead the differences between the genders to be almost nil.

许多研究的结论都证明它是无效的，并且发现性别之间的差异几乎为零。

conclusions /kənˈkluʒənz/ 结论 studies /ˈstədiz/ 研究 invalid /ˌɪnˈvæləd/ 无效的 instead /ˌɪnˈstɛd/ 反而 differences /ˈdɪfərənsɪz/ 差异

057

T here are, however, notable differences between individuals regardless of their gender.

然而，无论性别如何，个体之间都存在显着差异。

however /ˌhaʊˈɛvər/ 然而 notable /ˈnoʊtəbəl/ 值得注意的 differences /ˈdɪfərənsɪz/ 差异 individuals /ˌɪndəˈvɪʤəwəlz/ 个人 regardless /rəˈgɑrdləs/ 不管

058

The absurd criterion for judging a person's ability based on their gender needs to be abolished.

根据性别来判断一个人的能力的荒谬标准需要废除。

criterion /kraɪˈtɪriən/ 标准 judging /ˈʤəʤɪŋ/ 判断 ability /əˈbɪləˌti/ 能力 abolished /əˈbɑlɪʃt/ 废除

059

Until this is seen as being abnormal, the attempt to updated attitudes without removing the underlying cause of the societal values will be useless.

在这被视为异常之前，在不消除社会价值观的根本原因的情况下更新态度的尝试将是无用的。

abnormal /æbˈnɔrməl/ 异常 attempt /əˈtɛmpt/ 试图 updated /ˈəpˌdeɪtɪd/ 已更新 attitudes /ˈætəˌtudz/ 态度 removing /riˈmuvɪŋ/ 去除

docs.title: Unit 14 中国革命之父孙中山先生
Dr. Sun Yat-sen: Father of the Chinese Revolution
docs.text:
原文链接：Part 1 / Part 2

复习方式：先读英文，再看译文，最后只背本句下面的词和短语。

001

Dr. Sun Yat-sen held official political office for a total of only a few months in China, yet he had an impact so profound that it earned him the designation of Father of the Chinese Revolution.

孙中山先生在中国担任官方政治职务总共只有几个月，但他的影响却如此深远，以至于他被称为“中国革命之父”。

yat-sen /sɛn/ 中山 official /əˈfɪʃəl/ 官方的 political /pəˈlɪtɪkəl/ 政治的 profound /proʊˈfaʊnd/ 深刻的 designation /ˌdɛzɪgˈneɪʃən/ 指定

002

He was a man who is still much revered in China.

他是一位在中国仍然备受尊敬的人。

revered /rɪˈvɪrd/ 受人尊敬

003

His portrait can be seen in Tiananmen Square in Beijing.

在北京天安门广场可以看到他的肖像。

portrait /ˈpɔrtrət/ 肖像 tiananmen /tiˈɛnænˌmɛn/ 天安门

004

Sun was born in 1866 in Guangdong Province.

孙先生于1866年出生于广东省。

guangdong /gˈwɑŋˈdɔŋ/ 粤 province /ˈprɑvɪns/ 省

005

His ancestors were clans of farmers and shepherds.

他的祖先是农民和牧羊人。

ancestors /ˈænˌsɛstərz/ 祖先 farmers /ˈfɑrmərz/ 农民 shepherds /ˈʃɛpərdz/ 牧羊人

006

During his adolescent years, he attended school in Honolulu and Hong Kong.

青少年时期，他在檀香山和香港上学。

adolescent /ˌædəˈlɛsənt/ 青少年 attended /əˈtɛndəd/ 出席 honolulu /ˌhɑnəˈlulu/ 檀香山

007

In the latter city, he studied medicine, receiving an “A” in every subject in the program, an unprecedented feat at Hong Kong Medical College (later, the University of Hong Kong).

在后一个城市，他学习医学，并在课程中的每个科目中都获得了“A”，这在香港医学院（后来的香港大学）中是前所未有的壮举。

studied /ˈstədid/ 研究过 medicine /ˈmɛdəsən/ 药品 receiving /rɪˈsivɪŋ/ 接收 subject /ˈsəbʤɪkt/ 主题 program /ˈproʊˌgræm/ 程序

008

While in Hong Kong, Sun undertook conversion to Roman Catholicism.

在香港期间，孙皈依了罗马天主教。

undertook /ˌəndərˈtʊk/ 承担了 conversion /kənˈvərʒən/ 转换 catholicism /kəˈθɔləˌsɪzəm/ 天主教

009

Early in life, Sun developed contempt for the corruption of the Qing (Manchu) Dynasty.

孙早年就对清朝的腐败产生了蔑视。

developed /dɪˈvɛləpt/ 发达 contempt /kənˈtɛmpt/ 鄙视 corruption /kərˈəpʃən/ 腐败 dynasty /ˈdaɪnəsti/ 王朝

010

He was also vocal in denouncing foreign intrusions and aggression against China during the 19th century.

他还大声谴责19世纪外国对中国的入侵和侵略。

denouncing /dɪˈnaʊnsɪŋ/ 谴责 foreign /ˈfɔrən/ 外国的 intrusions /ˌɪnˈtruʒənz/ 入侵 aggression /əˈgrɛʃən/ 侵略 century /ˈsɛnʧəri/ 世纪

011

The opium war of 1839 to 1842 was a major testimony to China's inability to defend itself against outside aggression.

1839年至1842年的鸦片战争是中国无力抵御外来侵略的重要证明。

war /wɔr/ 战争 testimony /ˈtɛstɪˌmoʊni/ 见证 inability /ˌɪnəˈbɪlɪti/ 无力 outside /ˈaʊtˈsaɪd/ 外部 aggression /əˈgrɛʃən/ 侵略

012

By this period, Britain had developed a strong monopoly in the trade of many goods, including tea, salt, opium, and other commodities.

到了这个时期，英国已经在许多商品的贸易中形成了强大的垄断地位，包括茶叶、盐、鸦片和其他商品。

developed /dɪˈvɛləpt/ 发达 monopoly /məˈnɑpəli/ 垄断 trade /treɪd/ 贸易 including /ˌɪnˈkludɪŋ/ 包括 commodities /kəˈmɑdətiz/ 商品

013

This monopoly was exercised mostly through the British East India Company.

这种垄断主要是通过英国东印度公司行使的。

monopoly /məˈnɑpəli/ 垄断 exercised /ˈɛksərˌsaɪzd/ 行使 company /ˈkəmpəˌni/ 公司

014

Britain had been importing much from China, but was exporting little.

英国一直从中国进口大量商品，但出口很少。

importing /ˌɪmˈpɔrtɪŋ/ 输入 exporting /ɪkˈspɔrtɪŋ/ 出口

015

1911 年 10 月的武昌起义将孙中山带到了上海。

wuchang：武昌 brought /brɔt/ 带来 yat-sen /sɛn/ 中山

074

Shortly after the successful overthrow of the Qing Dynasty, Sun was elected Interim President of the new Republic of China in Nanking, the capital.

（译文待校）

shortly /ˈʃɔrtli/ 不久 successful /səkˈsɛsfəl/ 成功的 overthrow /ˈoʊvərθˌroʊ/ 推翻 dynasty /ˈdaɪnəsti/ 王朝 elected /ɪˈlɛktɪd/ 当选

075

This government immediately set out to develop a provisional(temporary) constitution.

（译文待校）

government /ˈgəvərnmənt/ 政府 immediately /ˌɪˈmiˌdiətli/ 立即地 develop /dɪˈvɛləp/ 发展 provisional /prəˈvɪʒənəl/ 临时 temporary /ˈtɛmpərˌɛri/ 暂时的

076

However, by February of 1912, Sun resigned as president to give way to Yuan Shikai, who brought with him a lot of support from the north, which provided the opportunity to unify greater parts of China.

（译文待校）

however /ˌhaʊˈɛvər/ 然而 february /ˈfɛbruˌɛri/ 二月 resigned /rɪˈzaɪnd/ 辞职了 president /ˈprɛzɪdənt/ 总统 brought /brɔt/ 带来

077

Also in 1912, the United League of China set up the Kuomingtang (KMT), the National Party of China.

（译文待校）

kuomingtang：国民党 national /ˈnæʃənəl/ 国家的

078

Yuan Shikai, in the meantime betrayed the republic and Sun's trust, by attempting to set himself up as a dictator.

（译文待校）

meantime /ˈminˌtaɪm/ 与此同时 betrayed /bɪˈtreɪd/ 被背叛 republic /riˈpəblɪk/ 共和国 attempting /əˈtɛmptɪŋ/ 尝试 dictator /ˈdɪkteɪtər/ 独裁者

079

Sun immediately proceeded in pursuit of Yuan but was unsuccessful and had to go into exile in Japan.

（译文待校）

immediately /ˌɪˈmiˌdiətli/ 立即地 proceeded /prəˈsidəd/ 继续进行 pursuit /pərˈsut/ 追求 unsuccessful /ˌənsəkˈsɛsfəl/ 不成功

080

In 1924, the Kuomingtang convened at Guangzhou to establish three principles to solidify and strengthen the republic and to unify the rest of China.

（译文待校）

kuomingtang：国民党 convened /kənˈvind/ 召集 guangzhou /gˈwæŋˌzu/ 广州 establish /ɪˈstæblɪʃ/ 建立 principles /ˈprɪnsəpəlz/ 原则

081

These principles included developing an alliance with Russia, helping farmers, workers, and bourgeoisie, and recommending a national conference to end the brutal, unequal treaties imposed by foreign nations.

（译文待校）

principles /ˈprɪnsəpəlz/ 原则 included /ˌɪnˈkludɪd/ 包括 developing /dɪˈvɛləpɪŋ/ 发展 alliance /əˈlaɪəns/ 联盟 helping /ˈhɛlpɪŋ/ 帮助

082

The result was “the Declaration of Beijing”, the last official act of Dr. Sun Yat-sen before liver cancer took his life in March of 1925.

（译文待校）

declaration /ˌdɛklərˈeɪʃən/ 宣言 official /əˈfɪʃəl/ 官方的 yat-sen /sɛn/ 中山

083

Sun Yat-sen was widely mourned as tributes came in from all over.

（译文待校）

yat-sen /sɛn/ 中山 mourned /mɔrnd/ 哀悼 tributes /ˈtrɪbjuts/ 贡品

084

Many intellectuals saw Sun as a man of action, a pragmatist, and not as a great intellectual.

（译文待校）

intellectuals /ˌɪntəˈlɛkʧuəlz/ 知识分子 pragmatist /ˈprægmətɪst/ 实用主义者 intellectual /ˌɪnəˈlɛkʧuəl/ 知识分子

085

Throughout his life, he was not above contradicting his own principles, or tolerating opposing views or parties to further his cause.

（译文待校）

contradicting /ˌkɑntrəˈdɪktɪŋ/ 矛盾的 principles /ˈprɪnsəpəlz/ 原则 tolerating /ˈtɑlərˌeɪtɪŋ/ 容忍 opposing /əˈpoʊzɪŋ/ 反对 parties /ˈpɑrtiz/ 聚会

086

For Sun, during these turbulent times, the end sometimes did seem to justify the means.

（译文待校）

turbulent /ˈtərbjələnt/ 动荡的 sometimes /ˈsəmˌtaɪmz/ 有时 justify /ˈʤəstəˌfaɪ/ 证明合法

087

His philosophy changed, over time, to meet changing needs.

（译文待校）

philosophy /fəˈlɑsəfi/ 哲学 changed /ʧeɪnʤd/ 改变了 changing /ˈʧeɪnʤɪŋ/ 改变

088

For many academics, Sun's career was not seen as the making of a myth, but as a real man dealing with real complex realities of his time.

（译文待校）

academics /ˌækəˈdɛmɪks/ 学者 dealing /ˈdilɪŋ/ 交易 complex /ˈkɑmplɛks/ 复杂的 realities /ˌriˈæləˌtiz/ 现实

089

His presence, inside and outside of China, dominated Chinese history during the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

（译文待校）

presence /ˈprɛzəns/ 在场 outside /ˈaʊtˈsaɪd/ 外部 dominated /ˈdɑməˌneɪtəd/ 占主导地位 history /ˈhɪstəri/ 历史 centuries /ˈsɛnʧəriz/ 世纪

090

He adopted and tailored western ideas to the Chinese experience, in order to create his vision of a new China.

（译文待校）

adopted /əˈdɑptəd/ 通过 tailored /ˈteɪlərd/ 量身定制 western /ˈwɛstərn/ 西 experience /ɪkˈspɪriəns/ 经验

091

Many academics also felt that Sun's western experiences greatly influenced his work and contributed to his predominant place in Chinese and world history.

（译文待校）

academics /ˌækəˈdɛmɪks/ 学者 western /ˈwɛstərn/ 西 experiences /ɪkˈspɪriənsɪz/ 经历 greatly /ˈgreɪtli/ 大大地 influenced /ˈɪnfluənst/ 影响

092

Before he died, he stated that the whole nation had to be awakened and united with those who treated them equally, and fight side by side with them.

（译文待校）

awakened /əˈweɪkənd/ 被唤醒 treated /ˈtritɪd/ 治疗过的 equally /ˈikwəli/ 同样地

093

Sun Yat-sen had received the respect of people throughout the world, even from non-communist sources.

（译文待校）

yat-sen /sɛn/ 中山 received /rɪˈsivd/ 已收到 respect /rɪˈspɛkt/ 尊重 non-communist /ˈnɑnˈkɑmjunɪst/ 非共产主义 sources /ˈsɔrsəz/ 来源

094

In China, he became a legend.

（译文待校）

095

When the Kuomingtang and the Communists split in 1927, both claimed to be heirs of his work.

（译文待校）

kuomingtang：国民党 communists /ˈkɑmjənəsts/ 共产主义者 claimed /kleɪmd/ 声称

096

No one can deny Sun Yat-sen his rightful place, not only in Chinese history but also in world history.

（译文待校）

yat-sen /sɛn/ 中山 rightful /ˈraɪtfəl/ 正当的 history /ˈhɪstəri/ 历史

097

He truly deserves the title and honour of Father of the Chinese Revolution.

（译文待校）

deserves /dɪˈzərvz/ 应得的 revolution /ˌrɛvəˈluʃən/ 革命

docs.title: The World Trade Organization(WTO) and China
docs.text:
原文链接：Part 1 / Part 2

复习方式：先读英文，再看译文，最后只背本句下面的词和短语。

001

As China has been admitted to the World Trade Organization (WTO), it is very apt at this time to compile some important data about this international organization.

（译文待校）

admitted /ədˈmɪtəd/ 承认 trade /treɪd/ 贸易 organization /ˌɔrgənəˈzeɪʃən/ 组织 apt /æpt/ 易于 compile /kəmˈpaɪl/ 编译

002

The conception of the WTO took place during the 1995 Uruguay round of talks of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT).

（译文待校）

conception /kənˈsɛpʃən/ 概念 uruguay /ˈjərəgˌweɪ/ 乌拉圭 general /ˈʤɛnərəl/ 一般的 agreement /əˈgrimənt/ 协议 tariffs /ˈtɛrəfs/ 关税

003

The WTO actually replaced GATT.

（译文待校）

actually /ˈæˌkʧuəli/ 实际上 replaced /ˌriˈpleɪst/ 被取代

004

This latter organization, a composite of many countries, was formed after the Second World War to preside over the stabilization of trade among nations.

（译文待校）

organization /ˌɔrgənəˈzeɪʃən/ 组织 composite /kəmˈpɑzət/ 合成的 countries /ˈkəntriz/ 国家 war /wɔr/ 战争 preside /prɪˈzaɪd/ 主持

005

The new organization, the WTO, is dedicated to allocating the resources of the world by using fairer trade practices and providing economic security for the more vulnerable, less developed nations.

（译文待校）

organization /ˌɔrgənəˈzeɪʃən/ 组织 dedicated /ˈdɛdəkeɪtəd/ 投入的 allocating /ˈæləˌkeɪtɪŋ/ 分配 resources /ˈrisɔrsɪz/ 资源 trade /treɪd/ 贸易

006

The WTO provides the apparatus for making this happen through increased cooperation among member countries.

（译文待校）

provides /prəˈvaɪdz/ 提供 apparatus /ˌæpərˈætəs/ 设备 increased /ˌɪnˈkrist/ 增加 cooperation /kˌwɔpərˈeɪʃən/ 合作 countries /ˈkəntriz/ 国家

007

The execution of such agreements will be instrumental in enhancing the esteem of less developed members and will provide a more stable infrastructure for profitable trade for members of the WTO.

（译文待校）

execution /ˌɛksəˈkjuʃən/ 执行 agreements /əˈgrimənts/ 协议 instrumental /ˌɪnstrəˈmɛnəl/ 工具性的 enhancing /ɛnˈhænsɪŋ/ 增强 developed /dɪˈvɛləpt/ 发达

008

Is there a way to describe in simple terms what this is all about, What underlies this international pursuit of free trade among nations, Students of introductory Economics would recognize the theory of “comparative advantage”.

（译文待校）

comparative advantage：比较优势 describe /dɪˈskraɪb/ 描述 underlies /ˌəndərˈlaɪz/ 底层 international /ˌɪnərˈnæʃənɑl/ 国际的 pursuit /pərˈsut/ 追求 trade /treɪd/ 贸易

009

Briefly, this economic theory states that a country can produce all or most goods and services more efficiently than most or all other countries, but still gain from specializing in production and trading with other nations.

（译文待校）

briefly /ˈbrifli/ 简要地 economic /ˌɛkəˈnɑmɪk/ 经济的 country /ˈkəntri/ 国家 produce /ˈproʊdus/ 生产 services /ˈsərvɪsɪz/ 服务

010

They not only receive economic benefits for themselves, but also help other countries achieve similar benefits in the process.

（译文待校）

receive /rɪˈsiv/ 收到 economic /ˌɛkəˈnɑmɪk/ 经济的 benefits /ˈbɛnəfɪts/ 好处 countries /ˈkəntriz/ 国家 achieve /əˈʧiv/ 达到

011

Let's look at a simple example.

（译文待校）

example /ɪgˈzæmpəl/ 例子

012

Assume that there are two countries, Alpha and Beta, that produce the same two products, bananas and office desks, and nothing else.

（译文待校）

countries /ˈkəntriz/ 国家 produce /ˈproʊdus/ 生产 products /ˈprɑdəkts/ 产品 bananas /bəˈnænəz/ 香蕉 nothing /ˈnəθɪŋ/ 没有什么

013

We will assume that each country has 200 units of productive resources (resources such as land, labour and capital, used in the production of bananas and desks).

（译文待校）

country /ˈkəntri/ 国家 productive /pərˈdəktɪv/ 富有成效的 resources /ˈrisɔrsɪz/ 资源 capital /ˈkæpɪtəl/ 首都 production /pərˈdəkʃən/ 生产

014

In this case we will use labour.

（译文待校）

015

Before trading each country, using the productive resources each has available, might produce the following combinations: Bananas（tons） Alpha 300 (100 units of labour) Beta 100(100 units) Totals 400 Desks Alpha 100 (100 units) Beta 25 (100 units) Totals 125 Assuming that each country used the same amount of productive resources in the production of both bananas and desks, you will notice that Alpha produced more bananas and more desks than Beta but produced desks more efficiently (higher ratio 4∶1) than bananas (3∶1).

（译文待校）

trading /ˈtreɪdɪŋ/ 贸易 country /ˈkəntri/ 国家 productive /pərˈdəktɪv/ 富有成效的 resources /ˈrisɔrsɪz/ 资源 available /əˈveɪləbəl/ 可用的

016

Alpha produced four times as many desks as Beta given equal units of resources (100 units) and three times as many bananas as Beta.

（译文待校）

produced /prəˈdust/ 产生的 resources /ˈrisɔrsɪz/ 资源 bananas /bəˈnænəz/ 香蕉

017

Alpha has a comparative advantage in producing desks and therefore could make economic gains by transferring some of its labour resources into the production of desks.

（译文待校）

comparative advantage：比较优势 producing /prəˈdusɪŋ/ 生产 therefore /ˈðɛrˌfɔr/ 所以 economic /ˌɛkəˈnɑmɪk/ 经济的 transferring /trænsˈfərɪŋ/ 转移 resources /ˈrisɔrsɪz/ 资源

018

If the two countries were agreeable to specialize and trade with each other, the following might be possible: Bananas（tons） Alpha 210(70 units) Beta 200(200 units) Total410 Desks Alpha 130(130 units) Beta 0(0 units) Total 130 This example shows that, by specialization by each partner, total production of bananas would increase from 400 tons to 410 tons and the production of desks would increase from 125 to 130 desks.

（译文待校）

countries /ˈkəntriz/ 国家 agreeable /əˈgriəbəl/ 令人愉快的 specialize /ˈspɛʃəˌlaɪz/ 专门化 trade /treɪd/ 贸易 following /ˈfɑloʊɪŋ/ 下列的

019

This means that more of each product would be available to both countries to share through specialization and trade.

（译文待校）

product /ˈprɑdəkt/ 产品 available /əˈveɪləbəl/ 可用的 countries /ˈkəntriz/ 国家 specialization /ˌspɛʃələˈzeɪʃən/ 专业化 trade /treɪd/ 贸易

020

This may be an oversimplification of the concept of comparative advantage, but it is the economic principle which explains why countries want more free trade, and why China wants to join the WTO.

（译文待校）

comparative advantage：比较优势 oversimplification /oʊvərˈsɪmplɪfɪˌkeɪʃən/ 简单化 concept /ˈkɑnsɛpt/ 概念 economic /ˌɛkəˈnɑmɪk/ 经济的 principle /ˈprɪnsəpəl/ 原则 explains /ɪkˈspleɪnz/ 解释

021

It also explains the United State's ambitious pursuit of freer trade arrangements throughout the world.

（译文待校）

explains /ɪkˈspleɪnz/ 解释 ambitious /æmˈbɪʃəs/ 雄心勃勃的 pursuit /pərˈsut/ 追求 trade /treɪd/ 贸易 arrangements /ərˈeɪnʤmənts/ 安排

022

Immersed for more than a decade in negotiations, the climax has been reached for China.

（译文待校）

immersed /ˌɪˈmərst/ 沉浸 gotiations：谈判 reached /riʧt/ 达到

023

Its official membership in the WTO commenced in December 2001.

（译文待校）

official /əˈfɪʃəl/ 官方的 membership /ˈmɛmbərˌʃɪp/ 会员资格 commenced /kəˈmɛnst/ 开始 december /dɪˈsɛmbər/ 十二月

024

It has not been an easy road to reach this goal and the country will now embark upon an even tougher road of more formidable challenges.

（译文待校）

country /ˈkəntri/ 国家 tougher /ˈtəfər/ 更强硬 formidable /ˌfɔrˈmɪdəbəl/ 强大 challenges /ˈʧælənʤɪz/ 挑战

025

Many issues surrounding China's bid are not only economic, but also social in nature.

（译文待校）

surrounding /sərˈaʊndɪŋ/ 周围 bid /bɪd/ 出价 economic /ˌɛkəˈnɑmɪk/ 经济的

026

For example, the United States has amplified the issue of human rights in discussions between itself and China.

（译文待校）

human rights：人权 example /ɪgˈzæmpəl/ 例子 amplified /ˈæmpləˌfaɪd/ 放大的 discussions /dɪˈskəʃənz/ 讨论

027

The reasons for this obsession over human rights are not readily evident, but in some quarters suggestions for it have been offered.

（译文待校）

human rights：人权 reasons /ˈrizənz/ 原因 obsession /əbˈsɛʃən/ 痴迷 readily /ˈrɛdəli/ 容易 evident /ˈɛvədənt/ 明显 quarters /kˈwɔrtərz/ 宿舍

028

Since the end of the Cold War, and the demise (or fall) of the Soviet Union, the United States has had no clear opponent to justify the work of its many agencies that were originally assimilated to deal with former Cold War opponents.

（译文待校）

war /wɔr/ 战争 opponent /əˈpoʊnənt/ 对手 justify /ˈʤəstəˌfaɪ/ 证明合法 agencies /ˈeɪʤənsiz/ 机构 originally /ərˈɪʤənəli/ 起初

029

The promotion of international human rights allegedly has filled part of this void, to become the major target of the new direction in American foreign policy, and it has become commonplace for China in particular.

（译文待校）

human rights：人权 promotion /pərˈmoʊʃən/ 晋升 international /ˌɪnərˈnæʃənɑl/ 国际的 allegedly /əˈlɛʤədli/ 据称 void /vɔɪd/ 空白 direction /dɪˈrɛkʃɪn/ 方向

030

It should be noted that there are some current members of the WTO that have worse human rights records than that of China but were not treated in the same manner.

（译文待校）

human rights：人权 current /ˈkɑrənt/ 当前的 members /ˈmɛmbərz/ 会员 records /ˈrɛkərdz/ 记录 treated /ˈtritɪd/ 治疗过的

031

Also, it is erroneous to suggest that the United States itself is completely innocent of human rights violations.

（译文待校）

human rights：人权 erroneous /ɛˈroʊniəs/ 错误 suggest /səˈʤɛst/ 建议 completely /kəmˈplitli/ 完全地 innocent /ˈɪnəsənt/ 清白的 violations /vaɪəˈleɪʃənz/ 违规行为

032

This is a major contradiction in current American foreign policy.

（译文待校）

contradiction /ˌkɑntrəˈdɪkʃən/ 矛盾 current /ˈkɑrənt/ 当前的 foreign /ˈfɔrən/ 外国的

033

It is also suggested that the real threat to the United States is that China is a huge country with a robust economy that has been growing by leaps and bounds over the last twenty years.

（译文待校）

by leaps and bounds：突飞猛进地 suggested /səˈʤɛstɪd/ 建议 country /ˈkəntri/ 国家 robust /roʊˈbəst/ 强壮的 economy /ɪˈkɑnəmi/ 经济 growing /groʊɪŋ/ 生长

034

Henceforth, a fear is growing that the potential economic strength of China will threaten the prevalent position of the United States in world affairs.

（译文待校）

henceforth /ˈhɛnsˈfɔrθ/ 今后 growing /groʊɪŋ/ 生长 potential /pəˈtɛnʃəl/ 潜在的 economic /ˌɛkəˈnɑmɪk/ 经济的 strength /strɛŋθ/ 力量

035

More recently, during the spy plane incident over Hainan, American President Bush changed the American position toward China from that of being a world partner (the approach of the Clinton Administration), to that of being a competitor or an opponent in international affairs.

（译文待校）

recently /ˈrisəntli/ 最近 spy /spaɪ/ 间谍 incident /ˈɪnsədənt/ 事件 president /ˈprɛzɪdənt/ 总统 changed /ʧeɪnʤd/ 改变了

036

This “bashing” propaganda about China is considered by many people a cover-up (or a smoke screen) for growing American insecurity in international affairs and this distortion is accumulative in the brain washed minds of the American people.

（译文待校）

bashing /ˈbæʃɪŋ/ 殴打 propaganda /ˌprɑpəˈgændə/ 宣传 considered /kənˈsɪdərd/ 经过考虑的 cover-up /ˈkəvərˌəp/ 掩饰 growing /groʊɪŋ/ 生长

037

It is also degrading to say the least.

（译文待校）

degrading /dɪˈgreɪdɪŋ/ 有辱人格的

038

It is like a champion football team that does not want to play fairly any more because it is afraid of losing.

（译文待校）

champion /ˈʧæmpiən/ 冠军 football /ˈfʊtˌbɔl/ 足球 because /bɪˈkəz/ 因为

039

It is the fear of being beaten fairly and decisively on the field, according to an agreed upon set of rules.

（译文待校）

decisively /dɪˈsaɪsɪvli/ 果断地 according /əˈkɔrdɪŋ/ 根据

040

This obsession with human rights has flared up in many areas of American foreign policy in recent months.

（译文待校）

human rights：人权 obsession /əbˈsɛʃən/ 痴迷 foreign /ˈfɔrən/ 外国的

041

This rash, sometimes graphic ChinaBashing attitude is probably driven, in part, by powerful economic interests in the United States.

（译文待校）

rash /ræʃ/ 皮疹 sometimes /ˈsəmˌtaɪmz/ 有时 graphic /ˈgræfɪk/ 形象的 bashing /ˈbæʃɪŋ/ 殴打 attitude /ˈætəˌtud/ 态度

042

The positions of these powerful interests will be seriously threatened by China's entry into the WTO.

（译文待校）

positions /pəˈzɪʃənz/ 职位 powerful /ˈpaʊərfəl/ 强大的 interests /ˈɪntərɪsts/ 兴趣 seriously /ˈsɪriəsli/ 严重地 threatened /θˈrɛtənd/ 受到威胁

043

These industries, if they are forced to face stronger competition, fear losing their shares of their respective markets.

（译文待校）

industries /ˈɪndəstriz/ 行业 stronger /ˈstrɔŋgər/ 更强 competition /ˌkɑmpəˈtɪʃən/ 竞赛 respective /rɪˈspɛktɪv/ 各自 markets /ˈmɑrkɪts/ 市场

044

These same interests also heavily support political parties financially and therefore have some indirect influence over government policies.

（译文待校）

docs.title: In Another World
docs.text:
Here I am, in China,half way arWound the world from home. As I look at my clock and calculate the time back home I realize that half a world away, people are busy getting ready for a wedding.The bride is my niece, a person I first met when she was three days old.

I think back to the first time I had the opportunity to become acquainted with my niece. As my sister cradled her in her arms, the infant girl clasped her mother's outstretched finger.My intuition told me that her temperament would be a sunny disposition, a joy to people around her.As she grew, the cute little girl had an infectious laugh that started as a small grin, then became a giggle and grew louder and louder until it triggered a response from all the people around her and they joined in.As an adolescent, she studied hard and enjoyed welldeserved success in secondary school as she interacted with her peer group.After receiving her high school diploma, she chose nursing as her career.From the beginning of the young couples romance it was evident that they were compatible and were completely intrigued with each other.

The couple had an engagement party when I was at home in Canada a few months ago.The party was in the form of a picnic in a beautiful rose garden. To celebrate and to toast their future, we drank champagne. As they posed under an arch covered with climbing roses,we snapped pictures for their photo album.The couple decided on a fall wedding.

Plans for the wedding day were activated immediately.The decisions about the forthcoming event were shared by the whole family.A close friend of the family was contacted and invited to sing a solo just prior to the ceremony.The day before the ceremony, a rehearsal would take place so that the remainder of the details could be looked after and attended to.The planning that takes place beforehand for one of these events and all the work that the big day entails, with many people collaborating to make the event run smoothly, are immense. The conscientious attention to detail will be evident to the spectators of this event.I can imagine the excitement and emotions of the family today.

The time is near.The ceremony will begin in 3 short hours.The bride will be radiant as she comes down the aisle escorted by her father.She will wear her grandmother's pearls as an accessory.Her veil will be the same one as her cousin wore last year.As is customary, under her garments she will wear a blue garter.As part of the tradition of Canadian weddings, she will be wearing something old (the pearls), something new (her gown), something borrowed (the veil) and something blue (the garter).As the first chords of the wedding march are played (a melody familiar to all), the congregation will rise.Gasps will be heard as they catch a glimpse of the bride in her gorgeous wedding gown.The mother of the bride will calmly view this whole event, though tears will blur her vision.She will be overcome with sentiment at her daughter's apparent happiness.The picture will be one that will embody hope for the future of humanity.

As the couple exchange wedding vows they will be affirming their love and making a commitment to each other. All the spectators are there to wish them well.

As the time approaches, I think back to other family weddings over many years.

My older sisters were all married in the same church and as brides they carried a white Bible decorated with tiny roses. The receptions for their weddings were all held in the same church basement, as there was no large banquet hall in the local area.

The feast was usually catered by a group of church members.Today's wedding reception will be held in an arena that will be decorated with just the right amount of fall flowers in wonderful arrays to give it dignity yet a touch of glamour.

The table decorations will be a masterpiece.One of the table decorations will be small pumpkins, used as containers for flowers that were collected from family gardens, surrounded by a large wreath made from long stalks of wheat. There will be a few coloured leaves placed inside the wreath.

Maybe they will use oak and maple leaves to show the splendour of the autumn colours. The colour of the outfits that the bridesmaids are wearing will be fall colours as well. The ingenious decorations will be appreciated by the many guests attending the festivities. At each place setting there will be a special paper napkin with the bride and groom's name printed on it and the date of their wedding. It will be carefully folded placed on top and of a linen napkin. This will be one of the souvenirs the guests will have to commemorate the special wedding day.

Also at each place will be a few after dinner mints for the guests. A miniature tree will also be placed at each persons place. The intent is for the guests to take the little tree home and transplant it to a special place. In this way, our environment is also improved and the tree will become a living tribute to the young couple.

The groom will carry her across the threshold as is customary for a young couple as they begin their new life together. The honeymoon plans will take them to the west coast of Canada.They will have a week of privacy far away from friends and family. They will inhabit a condominium in the town of Whistler, British Columbia, in the Rocky Mountains. They will feel as if they are royalty living in a mansion in this little bit of paradise on earth. Thereafter, they will return home to Ontario where they will reside.Their original plan to spend their honeymoon on board a yacht in the Mediterranean Sea was abandoned when world circumstances dictated that our country Canada was a safer choice.

Earlier this month, as I thought about the forthcoming marriage, and knew that I would be unable to attend, I decided to write a message to the young couple.The intent was that the message would be read aloud during the wedding reception. In the message, I wished them well and urged them to cherish each other every day.

docs.title: Let's Dress Up——It's Halloween
docs.text:
From early childhood getting dressed up is connected with a special pastime in North America,called Halloween.

Halloween is celebrated on the last night of October, when the air is crisp and snow is not far off. Every young child is acquainted with this exciting tradition.On the last day of October when dinner is finished,children hurry to dress up in a costume. Darkness comes early at this time of year and caution must be practiced, foremost by the children who are going from house to house, “trick or treat”.

Parents warn their children not to dart out in front of cars. In all the excitement it is easy for children to become distracted and ignore safety rules.Planning what your costume will be, ahead of time, is part of the fun of the evening. Many mothers will spend time fabricating outfits for their little girls who suddenly turn into circus clowns, beautiful ballet dancers or weird colorful bugs. Fathers may help their sons construct a costume of foil armor.

Little boys often enjoy pretending they are in the army so on Halloween it is possible to see squads of lieutenants and sergeants marching along in the dark. We affiliate this celebration with the supernatural so some children may choose to wear a skeleton costume bearing a skull and crossbones, or even a monster costume. The choice of wardrobe for the evening is really limitless. Witches can be seen riding on broomsticks across well illuminated intersections. Earlier in the evening they may have concocted a witch's brew to quench their thirst for their arrival home.

Ghosts can be heard groaning and moaning while they glide along city streets. Beautiful butterflies flutter by on their way to a party. Pirates carrying swords and pistols roam about, patches over one eye. Small aliens search for a new home here on Earth. Wearing a cape and mask allows a child to become Superman for a few hours and enter the world of fantasy.

An ethnic flavor is introduced as a band of gypsies dance along under a bright full moon.Of course you can always see a certain number of Native American costumes, the buckskin jackets and dresses decorated with fringe and beads.Some youngsters choose to decorate only their faces with grease paint instead of wearing masks. In many ways this is safer for a child, making visibility clearer. At the same time a mask allows them to remain anonymous to all but their closest friends.

Usually, on the night before Halloween, family members gather together to carve a pumpkin. On Halloween night the candle lit face of the pumpkin shines from each home welcoming the little ghosts and goblins to call. Parents usually escort small children around their own neighborhood helping to keep them safe. Small children only visit random houses, their parent's friends mostly, while older children knock at every door.Crowding onto the front porch of the house the children rap at the door and chant the refrain “trick or treat”.

Householders distribute candies, apples, peanuts, or any edible treat into decorated wooden six quart baskets, or plastic bags. They may be asked to recite a poem or sing a song before receiving their treat. Some lucky children may receive cookies from a freshly baked batch of chocolate chip cookies. On arriving home the children will dump all the junk candy out onto the floor to examine their loot. Usually there is a great racket as brothers and sisters compare what goodies they have collected.Adults, too, like to join in Halloween celebrations by attending small house parties or large group gatherings at halls or arenas. They may play the old traditional games such as bobbing for apples, which float in tubs of water, telling ghost stories and visiting a haunted house.

Everyone seems to get enjoyment from being slightly afraid.

If you live in the country the hooting of an owl or even the howl of a wolf underlines the spooky atmosphere of Halloween evening. Clouds scuttle across the face of the moon and the flap of a bird's wings can be heard as it settles on the bare branches of a tree. Eyes gleam in the night as a black cat crosses your path. Bats swoop about in the dark startling those who are nervous.On this evening it is not necessary to be extravagant to have a good time.

A little imagination and a sense of fun will create a memory of Halloween night for many years.

docs.title: Gardening
docs.text:
One of the quiet joys of life in the southern part of Ontario, Canada, is gardening.

Whether pursued as a hobby or solely to improve the esthetic value of one's home, the pleasure derived is only exceeded by the therapeutic benefit. The exercise involved in working in a garden is helpful in keeping people in good physical condition.It has become a ritual for homeowners to spend late winter weekends browsing through seed catalogues while sitting on their couch. They make lists of items they wish to purchase and often make notations right on the catalogue as they make decisions about this year's garden.If they order early, there is usually a discount coupon, allowing a percentage of the cost to be deducted from the price.

Often the coupon needs to be detached from the catalogue and mailed to the company along with the order. This is an extra bonus for the consumer. The investment cost required is nominal when the amount of pleasure generated is considered. The seed companies will usually warrant the plants, and often a refund is offered if the plants do not thrive. The shipment from the seed company's warehouse is awaited with eager anticipation. Its appearance means that spring will soon arrive.

The glossy pages of the catalogues provide a preview of the visual delights that can be grown. Pictures show an array of flowers that dazzle the eye. There are monochromatic displays as well as others that are a fusion of the complete spectrum of the rainbow's colors. Also included in the publication are pictures and descriptions of vegetables, shrubs, and trees.

Avid gardeners subscribe to magazines that specialize in articles and ads about this enjoyable pastime and people literally read each issue from cover to cover.Descriptions of plants include implicit instructions on whether to plant them in sun or shade. Specification as to the amount of irrigation required is also stated.

Elaborate irrigation systems are sometimes installed or a trench for improving the water flow is used. Controls are needed on irrigation systems because if the ground becomes too saturated the soil in the garden will be too muddy to allow anyone to work in it until it dries out.

If there is too much water constantly, the garden will become a swamp and impossible to cultivate. (Many people like to preserve the natural habitat of birds and wildlife in a marsh. These areas are usually protected by the government and although important to our environment, are not considered gardens.)

Geographic location is important for plants.

Certain plants are only suitable for propagation close to the equator. Others need to be several degrees of latitude away from the equator. Longitude is also a factor and most companies clearly state the conditions that will provide the optimum chances for the plants survival.Canadians grow tulips imported from Holland and they do well in the Southern Ontario climate.Because it is late spring before plants can survive outdoors in Southern Ontario, it is common for people to start their plants indoors.

Seeds are planted in small containers and continue to grow indoors until the appropriate size is achieved. Sometimes ultraviolet light is used to encourage plant growth. When the mercury rises and the danger of frost is past, the plants are then transplanted to the garden or to a flowerbed.

Plants are nourished from the soil, but to provide optimum food, fertilizer can be applied to encourage vigorous growth. Sometimes fertilizer is diluted with water while other kinds are dispersed with a spreader that flings the fertilizer granules in a small radius around the plants. The water soluble fertilizer will then be absorbed into the soil the next time it rains. Just as people need minerals, such as calcium and zinc, to be healthy, plants also need minerals but phosphorous and nitrogen are better food for them.

Some gardeners plan their garden with meticulous attention to detail.They choose colors that will complement each other and design their garden as if they were painting on a canvas.

Others are more spontaneous and simply visit a nursery and purchase plants that appeal to them. Often gardeners have a trademark plant that is their specialty.

Perhaps they enjoy the velvet texture of the leaves, or maybe the flower's color attracts them.The varieties of gardens are endless. Terrace gardening has become popular. With a herbal garden, cooks enjoy being able to use fresh herbs from their garden to add zest to their favorite dishes. They simply visit their garden and clip a few pieces of the herb they wish to use.

Every garden is as individual as its owner.

Gardens come in all shapes and sizes. Some are in the shape of a rectangle, while others are circular or irregular in shape. Some gardeners like the appearance of an asymmetrical shape while others work to achieve symmetry in their gardens.

For vegetable gardens, the most popular shape is rectangular and vegetables are usually planted in a linear fashion. This method makes it easier to cultivate between the rows of plants.

You could mistake some gardens for a meadow when the gardener chooses to include only wildflowers as a choice of vegetation. Including a pond in a garden is popular too.Entrepreneurs are always looking for innovations and gadgets that will attract the attention of devoted gardeners and induce them to spend their money. It has become a huge industry in the last few years, as the baby boomers reach retirement age and have more time to pursue hobbies such as gardening.

There are new products patented every year to tempt the gardener.It is possible to buy a kit that contains a complete set of tools needed by the home gardener. Unfortunately, often the quality is poor and the product is a fraud. Instead of having something good to work with, the purchase turns out to be junk.If you want to flatter a gardener, and boost their ego at the same time, summon up the courage to simply ask if you can swap plants.

Of course, it will give them a thrill if you also compliment them on the hardiness of their plants as compared to yours. They might even try to console you on your lack of competence as a gardener because your plants are not as sturdy as their plants.Irrespective of the competence of the gardener, anyone who augments the number of plants grown is helping to conserve our planet by averting erosion.

This pays great dividends for everyone as it also serves to protect the ozone layer.Some people erect barricades to keep small animals from attacking the plants. Squirrels love to dig up flower bulbs. They find them a tasty treat.It is common to see ceramic fixtures or figurines in a garden. Even the untrained eye can tell that the imitations are a fake, yet properly placed, they add to the intrinsic beauty.

A rain gauge, attached by a bracket to a fence, is a common sight and is used to enable the gardener to diagnose the moisture level of the soil around the plants and determine if they need more water. If nature does not provide enough rain, then the gardener will use a plastic or rubber hose to provide more irrigation. With a twist of a knob, or by moving a lever, the thirst of the plants for moisture can be quenched.What greater pleasure, than to work in your garden and as you clip the overgrown plants back to size or prune branches of fruit trees, hear the buzz of bees?

You know that they are enjoying your garden as they extract the pollen from the blooms. You relish the feeling that you are one with nature. The hum of insects as they share the garden is more pleasurable than music from a stereo or a symphony to a devoted gardener.

In addition,the scent of the flowers is an integral part of the joy of spending time working in a garden.The irony of the situation is that nature sometimes conspires against the gardener, and a hailstorm can riddle beautiful plants, shredding their leaves in minutes. Hurricanes can uproot even the largest trees although this is an event that seldom occurs in Southern Ontario. Tornadoes are more likely in this area.Parasites can attack plants and threaten their survival.

Any number of things can become a plague. It is often difficult to discern exactly what it is that is destroying the precious plants. Any number of complications can shatter the gardener's dreamof surpassing last year's accomplishment. An authentic gardener will not brood about the disappointment for long. Even as the disaster is occurring, you might overhear the gardener murmur “There's always next year.”

docs.title: A Canadian Family Story
docs.text:
My story begins in Newfoundland where my brother and I were born during the Second World War.

The island of Newfoundland, which was originally a British colony, became the newest province of Canada in 1949, the same year that the People's Republic of China was born.Our mother was born and raised in Newfoundland.

During the War (World War II), she worked in St. John's, the capital city, where she met a young Canadian sailor from Ontario. He was a member of the crew of a Royal Canadian Navy ship that was part of one of the convoys that escorted supply ships across the Atlantic Ocean to Europe during the war. They fell in love and subsequently, got married.

The rest is history, so to speak.

Our family moved to Ontario in late 1945, just after the war http://ended.In 1999, acting on impulse, my brother and I decided to take our mother to Newfoundland for a visit. It had been almost fifty years since we had last visited our mother's outport (remote or very rural island village) where she grew up. It was also the 50th anniversary of Newfoundland's becoming part of Canada.

In 1950, I was six and my brother was five when we last visited our mother's childhood home. At that time, Ireland's Eye was a vibrant, quaint fishing village hugging the rocky shore of a small, enclosed harbour. There was no electricity. There were no roads, no automobiles, and few signsof automation of any type. There were oil lamps and wood stoves in the homes and mere sootpaths between the aggregate of small communities on the hilly island, also named Ireland's Eye. We can still see and hear the inboard motorboats, putt putting (sound of engines) into the harbour, hauling their day's catch of fish. The image of hardy fishermen with pitchforks hoisting and tossing the codfish up to the stilted platforms from the bowels of the boats is still quite vivid. The aroma of salted, drying codfish, lingers still.

What I remember best, of almost half a century ago,was going out with my Uncle Fred in his boat to fish. That particular day, we were huddled together and lashed to other boats, just outside of the harbour. I can still hear the lively gossip between my uncle and the other fishermen, above the rippling and splashing of the waves against the hulls of the boats. I remember the boats heaving periodically, on the huge gently rolling waves.

My Uncle Fred had only one arm, but amazingly, he could do everything as if he had two hands. He could even roll a cigarette and light it.These are my memories of the quaint Newfoundland glory days gone by. It was a very hard life in those out ports, but a life romantically cherished by most of those who lived it.

Our mother was not feeling up to the trip at the time we were ready to leave, but insisted that my brother and I go on this odyssey. We would later provide her with pictures, a written account, and videotape of the trip.

Although we toured other parts of Newfoundland, including an overnight stay on the French Islands of St. Pierre and Miquilon, just off the south coast of Newfoundland, our main objective was to visit Ireland's Eye. This necessitated finding water transportation. We managed to arrange for a boat to take us on the half hour trip to the island. As it turned out, the married couple who ferried us over to the island was actually a couple of our distant cousins, whom we had never met.

We had intended to have our cousins drop us off on the island and pick us up a few hours later. However, either because we were newly found cousins, or they were typically hospitable Newfoundlanders, or they thought that my brother and I would get lost, they wanted to stay with us. Probably all three factors influenced their decision. They were absolutely fabulous.They got caught up in what my brother and Iwere trying to do. They were very knowledgeable about the island and the people who had once lived there. Clutching a narrative of the island, written by another of our cousins, the forgotten history of that special place became more coherent to the four of us.

As we entered Ireland's Eye's small harbour, which was guarded, by a family of hawks in a nest high on a rocky point, a weird sensation came over us. There, in front of us,was the place we visited fifty years before, and about which we had heard and read so much throughout our adult lives. We thought, what an aesthetically breathtaking sight!The glittering sun, on that day, gave everything a picturepostcard image. This was indeed a slice of paradise.

The ruins of a few remaining buildings that dotted the hillsides and shoreline and the once dominant St. Georges Church on the hill at the end of the harbour, aroused in us an exciting sense of history and of our heritage.

Looking out over the harbour from the hill by the church at the extinct community, revived memories of fifty years before.With a greater clarity of the knowledge of the area, we walked from the church a little farther inland to what used to be the post office and the school that our mother attended, the skeletal shells of which were still standing precariously. From there, stopping periodically to eat some edible berries, we struggled behind our cousins through the heavily brush and shrub covered footpaths to Black Duck Cove to visit the cemetery where our grandmother, whom we never knew, was buried.

This sacred ground was in very bad condition, with many badly corroded gravestones buried under brush and long grass.

After searching for a few minutes in the midst of tangled vegetation, we found our grandmother's resting place beside which we paid our respects. It was a good thing that our cousins stayed with us, as the footpaths that traversed the island, were overgrown with brush.

It would have been virtually impossible for my brother and me, to walk to the other communities on the island.We made our way back to the church on the hill and descended to the boat for a half hour boat ride to the other side of the island.

Sailing through a number of islets, we arrived at what remains of the small village of Traytown, where our grandparents had lived. There, we met some more long lost relatives at a small cottage. One, a bit of an eccentric, who now lives in Toronto but takes summer refuge in Traytown, showed us the remnants of what had once been our grandparents'house.

The Pasture

Night settled, thick with the acrid odors of gunpowder and blood.

No moon meant firing at muzzle flashes, an inexact method by which to combat one's foe, but the enemy had no advantage either. With artillery fire blanketing the field of battle, Jack had no opportunity to go to Mike's aid.He poked his head over the rim of the trench to see if he could spot Mike's corpse. He knew he was dead. He had heard his scream of pain when he was hit. His agonized moans had grown weaker and less frequent and finally ceased about ten minutes ago.

The regiment had been under heavy bombardment for two days,without respite. He had been too late to stop Mike as he propelled himself out of the foxhole and staggered as he hit the muddy terrain.

In hindsight, he should have seen it coming. Mike had started to break yesterday. He was becoming bizarre, talking about his patriotic duty to expel the enemy from these shores. Paradoxically, just before he hopped over the edge of the trench he scorned the day he had heeded the call to enlist.It pained him to realize that his one friend in this ungodly war had betrayed him by dying. Soldiers don't often make friends with one another, knowing they might die. He and Mike were different. They had known each other since they were children.

Mike was the best man when Jack and Lily walked down the aisle just a week before they left the dock and crossed the channel to engage the enemy.Clouds tumbled and overlapped one another as the wind began to freshen. It was getting colder now. The prospect of another night of rain, or perhaps even snow, made Jack quiver with dread.

Blood tinged water was beginning to crust over with ice. He could feel his toes and fingers stiffen as the temperature dropped. Maybe Mike was better off than he. At least the cold wouldn't bother him any more.Suddenly, comets of light began to streak across the night sky. They were using flares! The increased tempo of cannon fire coming from the left flank, shattering the earth around them,could only mean the enemy had sensed their weakness, and was coming in for the kill. They were heading straight for the underbelly!Jack's rifle misfired.

The whole corps had been issued new guns a few days before this campaign had started. It wasn't long before they discovered that the alloy used in the barrels couldn't endure prolonged firing, causing the shell casings to adhere in the bore. How could he repel the enemy without a weapon?Jack felt a stab of pain in his right thigh. The ground around him ruptured.

Jerking from side to side, he tried to dodge falling rocks and the clods of dirt raining down upon him. He slumped into a prone posture as he felt himself shoved from behind by an unknown force that felt as if it might have been a racing locomotive.

The last thing he heard, before his world was overturned, was a chorus of screams.

“Am I dead? Where am I? Where is everybody?” Cognitively, Jack realized he was still functioning physiologically so that meant he was still alive, but for how long? He couldn't move.

Maybe the impact had fractured his spine and he was paralyzed. He tried，analytically，to assess the damage incurred by moving his limbs, one by one, in a clockwise direction, starting with his right arm. Everything appeared able to be mobilized but for some reason he couldn't get up off the ground. Everything went black again.

Jack led his horse by the reins as they stepped onto the overpass bridging the gap between the plateaus. In the distance, he could see a twelve point buck grazing in the pasture, silhouetted against the waning sunset.Out of nowhere, a bull came charging across the meadow toward him.

He tried to run but his feet were pegged to the bridge.Drifting in and out of consciousness, Jack tried to make sense of what had happened to him. He seemed to be in a cavity under the ground. The earth was compacted on his legs but he thought he might be able to rotate his body enough to make himself a little more comfortable.

Was that a shaft of light he could see through the groove between the fingers of his left hand covering his eyes? He groped to clear a tiny bit more space for himself. The shutters of his consciousness closed again.

The galaxy was being probed by lunar modules shuttling between Earth and the other planets. As a member of a federation of geologists, Jack and his team had to follow the seam of ore to its source, a pasture on a distant asteroid.Once again, Jack regained lucidity. “Wow,” he thought, “that was like a bad paperback novel about astronomy!” He sniffed the air.

It was foul with the smell of death but qualitatively able to sustain life.Why was it so quiet? Was he deaf? Was the battle over? Was everyone dead? The weight on his legs was becoming oppressive.Lily lay back in the soft, green grass of the pasture.

White daisies, golden brown-eyed Susans, prickly blue viper's bugloss, and frilly Queen Anne's lace surrounded her. She beckoned to him from what seemed like miles away. He hiked through the grass calling her name. She began to stroll away from him into the distance. He had to reach her! He loved her so!

If they couldn't marry, he would make her his mistress! Nothing could extinguish the flame of his love! He would cling to that until his dying day.Lying stationary was taking its toll on Jack's circulation. His feet and hands were numb. Something was tickling his nose.

He managed to tilt away from the irritant, whatever it was. He was so thirsty! He tried to lubricate his lips with saliva but had none. His bladder felt like a separate entity that would overflow. He could stall the urge to void no longer and allowed the urine to flow out of him.

What did it matter now?He was as good as dead anyway.The fort stood in the center of the pasture.

A moat filled with sharks protected its walls from any possible intruders. Jack pedaled his bicycle as fast as he could. The sharks whipped back and forth so quickly they created foam on the surface of the water. He had to cross the drawbridge before it was raised, segregating him from his regiment and his pregnant wife, Lily. She saw him approaching and skipped onto the bridge to greet him.

The bridge was rising. The sharks were in frenzy! He rode as if the hounds of hell were after him. He had to reach her!His right arm was wedged against a rock. No matter how hard he tried, he couldn't wrench it free. This was getting tiresome. He felt a stitch in his right side. That's all he needed now to die from a ruptured appendix!

He had wriggled enough to increase the size of the slot in which he was trapped. Were those voices he was hearing? He wasn't deaf!When he fought his way to the surface of consciousness once again, he was being carried on a litter over the inverted battlefield. Bodies were strewn everywhere. The stretcher bearers stumbled over the rough ground but maintained control of their human cargo as they made their way to the field hospital.

The fuse leading to the dynamite in the stern of the oil tanker burned so rapidly that Jack knew the ship would explode before he could reach the hatch to extinguish the flame. The olive green ship was almost within his reach when it blew up.He felt as if he were on a grill. His face was aflame. His body felt as if the skin had been ripped from it.He wanted to die before the pain grew worse.His forehead felt cool.

He opened his eyes slowly, painfully. A white-clad nurse sponged his face gently.

As she became aware of his gaze, she stopped her ministrations and offered him a sip of water.

“Take it easy,” she whispered.

“You mustn't drink too quickly. Too much, too fast will give you nasty cramps.”

Jack was aware of bandages on his muscular arms and casts on both legs. Intravenous tubing carried a clear fluid into his veins. Consciousness was still transient. Dreams of a strange pasture mingled with reality and continued to haunt his sleep. He understood he was on a hospital ward, but where? And how did he get here?The pretty young nurse was back.

“We cabled your wife. She knows you were injured but are on the mend.”

“How did they find me?” Jack asked.

“A patrol looking for survivors found you buried in the the foxhole. You were calling ‘Lily!’They started digging and there you were. You were stabilized at the field hospital before they could bring you here.We scrubbed you up and started to you with I.V. therapy.

You were very dehydrated and suffering from urinary retentionand renal failure. Your kidneys may never function normally again. The good news is that you survived,” she explained. A stray strand of hair fell across Jack's cheek hiding the tears that crept from his eyes. He was grateful to have his life back. He silently saluted his friend. Mike hadn't been so lucky.The cable from Lily arrived the next day.

“We have a son stop Born 05 Dec. stop Healthy stop Named him Michael stop I love you. Lily stop P.S. Dad bought the pasture and deeded it to Michael.”

docs.title: The Decision
docs.text:
